strings: Ink Supplies is an Alliance errand on behalf of Brother Paxton, a monastic scribe residing in Northshire Abbey. Needing a specialized mineral component to brew his fast-drying ink, Paxton sends an adventurer east into the embattled township of Lakeshire to secure Rethban ore from Foreman Oslow.

Brother Paxton takes immense pride in his literary craft, refusing to rely on standard inks for vital transcriptions like The Stresses of Iron. Instead, he brews a custom recipe noted for its resistance to smearing and its rapid drying time. The formula's chief flaw is that it dries out even in the pot if left unattended too long. Replenishing his stock requires raw Rethban iron ore, a distinctive mineral mined in the rocky reaches of the Redridge Mountains.

When travelers arrive in Lakeshire carrying Paxton's humble requisition, they find the settlement in no condition to indulge a distant monk. Foreman Oslow oversees the strained town laborers, who are wholly occupied with shoring up barricades, rebuilding ruined structures, and bracing against ongoing raids from the Blackrock orcs. Oslow has neither the men nor the patience to dig ore for Stormwind's scribes, leaving outsiders to brave the perilous Rethban Caverns on their own.
Why does Brother Paxton need iron ore for ink?

Brother Paxton utilizes a proprietary recipe designed to produce permanent, smear-proof script that dries almost immediately. Ground Rethban iron ore provides the crucial mineral pigment and setting qualities necessary for his distinct ink.

The quest highlights Rethban iron ore, a localized mineral deposit nestled high in the crags of Redridge.

Return to Kristoff concludes Brother Kristoff's search for the elusive tome, The Stresses of Iron. After journeying through Redridge to fetch ore for special ink and waiting on Northshire's scribes, the adventurer finally brings the borrowed volume back to the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind.

Brother Kristoff, stationed in Stormwind's Cathedral Square, needed access to a specialized metallurgical volume known as The Stresses of Iron. The pursuit of the work sent couriers across human lands, leading first to the Royal Library in Stormwind Keep and then deep into Northshire Abbey. At the abbey, Brother Paxton was busily copying the text by hand, delayed by a shortage of Rethban ore needed to craft scribe's ink. With the ore retrieved and the copy complete, Paxton finally surrenders the original volume for its return to the city.

In a kingdom constantly pressed by outside threats, the quiet work of Northshire's copyists remains vital to preserving civic and spiritual lore. Brother Paxton's request to apologize to Librarian Milton Sheaf highlights how thin the abbey's resources have worn. Valuable books must be meticulously duplicated stroke by stroke using mineral-rich inks before they can be released back into Stormwind's care, turning a simple book request into an arduous logistical errand.
What is the book The Stresses of Iron about?

The Stresses of Iron is a treatise on metallurgy and metalworking. Brother Kristoff sought it out for study in Cathedral Square, while the scribes at Northshire Abbey required an exact copy to preserve its knowledge.

The Royal Library lent the book to Brother Paxton so he could produce an illuminated copy for Northshire Abbey's archives. Scribes there preserve important texts by hand, but Paxton's progress stalled when he ran short of Rethban ore for specialized ink.

Brother Kristoff is a member of the Clergy of the Holy Light stationed in Cathedral Square outside the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind. He requested the book and offers spiritual blessings in gratitude.
Milton Sheaf is the head librarian residing in Stormwind Keep's Royal Library. He originally permitted the loan of The Stresses of Iron and grew impatient over the lengthy delay in its return.

A simple errand for the clergy showcases how the Church of the Holy Light maintains, preserves, and distributes crucial scholarship throughout the kingdom.
Even seemingly trivial academic exchanges rely on safe roadways between Stormwind Keep, Northshire, and the embattled Redridge Mountains.

Foreman Oslow directs adventurers into the Rethban Caverns of Redridge to retrieve a peculiar dark mineral. While too soft to forge reliable armor or weapons, its unique pigmentation makes it indispensable to the scribes of Northshire Abbey for crafting specialized ink.

Rethban Ore is named after its discoverer, Bart Rethban. Unlike common iron or copper, this ore holds little value at an armorer's anvil—when smelted down, the resulting metal lacks the tensile strength required for sturdy weapons or plate. Its true value lies in its raw, dark, flat coloration, which monks and scribes prize as a pigment base for rich manuscript dyes.

The primary deposits of the mineral lie within the Rethban Caverns, nestled in the northern mountains of Redridge. Unfortunately for the stoneworkers of Lakeshire, the local miners have abandoned the cavern. A fierce band of Redridge gnolls has seized the tunnels, putting gnoll drudgers to work chipping away at the rocky veins for their own crude purposes.

Brother Paxton, a monk residing within the quiet walls of Northshire Abbey, depends on this pigment to reproduce historic texts. His current undertaking—a transcribed copy of the treatise 'The Stresses of Iron'—has ground to an abrupt halt without the proper dye, sending messengers and adventurers deep into gnoll-infested territory to secure the raw stone.
What is Rethban Ore used for?

While it is too weak when smelted to forge durable weapons or armor, its dark, flat color makes it an excellent base pigment for inks and dyes. Scribes such as Brother Paxton in Northshire Abbey rely on it to illuminate and transcribe historic manuscripts.

The errand highlights how stretched the Kingdom of Stormwind's supply lines are, requiring monastery scribes to rely on traveling adventurers to fetch basic writing supplies from war zones.
Miners can extract Rethban Ore directly from cavern veins with a pick, bypassing the need to scavenge raw chunks from gnoll drudgers.
Preserving historical manuscripts at Northshire Abbey is a sacred duty for Stormwind's scholars, who work to restore knowledge lost during the First and Second Wars.

Further Concerns is an Alliance courier quest dispatched by Marshal Dughan in Goldshire to investigate rumors of an amphibious threat. The marshal sends you eastward across Elwynn Forest to consult Guard Thomas at the river crossing. It shifts your attention from central garrison duties to the worsening security crisis along the eastern frontier.

While central Elwynn Forest struggles under the weight of banditry and vermin, alarming rumors have begun circulating about aquatic creatures creeping along the riverbanks. Marshal Dughan, commanding the garrison at Goldshire, refuses to dismiss the panic outright. Rather than pulling guards away from town, he sends travelers eastward aboard a fresh mount to consult Guard Thomas, the sentry posted at the bridge spanning the eastern river toward Redridge.

Guard Thomas has held the bridge outpost for over a week, witnessing firsthand what Goldshire's leadership could only suspect. Semi-intelligent, hostile murlocs have established camps all along the waterways of eastern Elwynn. With Stormwind's army absent and local garrisons pinned down protecting town walls and supply lines, rural bridgeheads like Thomas's post are left critically isolated against this encroaching peril.

Master Mathias Shaw directs an investigator to seek out an unconventional contact in Stormwind's Trade District. Because noble corruption shields powerful traitors from standard legal justice, the spymaster reluctantly relies on the intelligence network of the city's finest cheesemonger.

Following the discovery that Lord Gregor Lescovar and the assassin Marzon the Silent Blade maintain direct ties to the Defias Brotherhood, Master Mathias Shaw faces an intelligence dead end. With Edwin VanCleef dead in the Deadmines and Bazil Thredd eliminated in the Stockade, no living bandit leaders remain to testify. Furthermore, Lescovar's aristocratic status and extensive political ties place him effectively beyond the reach of standard Royal Guard justice and formal SI:7 warrants.

To pierce the defenses of a Stormwind noble, Shaw directs his agent to Elling Trias, the proprietor of Trias' Cheese in the Trade District. While outwardly a temperamental merchant known across the city for imported wedges and wheels, Trias runs an independent network of eyes and ears that rivals SI:7 itself. Shaw loathes calling upon his former colleague, but unmasking treason inside Stormwind Keep demands methods beyond official royal channels.

Elling Trias is far more than a simple cheesemonger. While he runs Trias' Cheese near the Trade District entrance, he maintains an independent, far-reaching underground intelligence web. Shaw loathes asking him for assistance, but SI:7 requires unconventional means to move against a nobleman who sits out of reach of standard law enforcement.

Lord Lescovar is a high-ranking Stormwind nobleman with deep connections across the House of Nobles. With Edwin VanCleef slain in the Deadmines and Bazil Thredd eliminated in the Stockade, SI:7 has no surviving high-ranking Defias witnesses whose confessions would legally stick to an aristocrat.

This task demonstrates how the corruption of the House of Nobles paralyzes Stormwind's internal security while King Varian Wrynn remains missing.

The Runed Scroll is a curious document tied with a silvery ribbon found in the wilds of Kalimdor. Its formal appearance suggests military or administrative communications originating from the night elves across the border. Discovering it leads Horde scouts directly to the Mor'shan Rampart to warn the guards of northern activity.

Wrapped tightly with an ornate silvery ribbon, the scroll immediately marks itself as something foreign to the rough leathers and parchment favored in the Barrens. Its fine craft and script point toward the night elves nestled beneath the dense canopies of Ashenvale just to the north. In a territory contested along every ridge and road, an intercepted missive is of paramount strategic value to the Horde's front lines.

Rather than sending the scroll across the plains to the Warchief in Orgrimmar, any adventurer with battlefield sense recognizes the urgency of local command. At the Mor'shan Rampart, stationed right where the red dirt of the Barrens yields to the lush forests of Ashenvale, the orc warrior Kadrak maintains watch over border incursions. Delivering this scroll provides the Rampart's outpost with crucial intelligence regarding night elf troop movements.
It is an official, finely crafted document tied with a silvery ribbon, indicating night elf origin. It contains intelligence regarding their movements or plans along the border with the Barrens.

Every intercepted piece of Alliance intelligence protects the lumber crews and border sentries defending the gateway into Ashenvale.
The Warsong Clan's expansion into Ashenvale depends heavily on border defense at the Mor'shan Rampart, making night elf missives vital news.

Horde Presence is a military strike commissioned by the orc Kadrak at the border of the Barrens and Ashenvale. Prompted by an intercepted missive, the Horde sends a champion high into Stonetalon Peak to eliminate the dryad Rynthariel and plant a Horde banner directly inside the Talon Den.

Guarding the northern boundary of the Barrens, Kadrak stands watchful against encroachments from the Alliance and the night elves. When a messenger carrying a runed scroll is cut down, Kadrak decodes the missive and traces its origin to Rynthariel the Keymaster, an influential dryad stationed in Stonetalon Peak. Rather than merely defending the mountain passes, Kadrak chooses an aggressive response to deter any future scouts from probing Horde territory.

The mission sends Horde warriors deep into the Talon Den, a cavernous redoubt overlooking Stonetalon Peak. Slaying Rynthariel strikes a direct blow against local night elf coordination, but the act is punctuated by planting Kadrak's Horde banner within the cave itself. By leaving their red standard fluttering in the heart of dryad territory, the Horde intends to signal clearly that incursions into the Barrens will be answered with decisive violence.
Who is Kadrak and why does he order this strike?

Kadrak is an orc warrior stationed at the northern border outpost between the Barrens and Ashenvale. Responsible for securing Horde lands against foreign encroachment, he orders a preemptive retaliation when he discovers Alliance messengers slipping through nearby passes.
kadrak | who is kadrak | kadrak purpose

Rynthariel is a dryad leader residing in the Talon Den atop Stonetalon Peak. She penned the runed scroll carried by the intercepted messenger, coordinating Alliance and sentinel movements across the mountain corridors.
rynthariel | rynthariel the keymaster | talon den boss

The Talon Den is a subterranean cavern complex located on the western slopes of Stonetalon Peak, nestled high in the Stonetalon Mountains.

Planting the flag serves as a psychological warning. Kadrak wants the night elves and the Alliance to see the red Horde banner standing over their fallen leader, ensuring they hesitate before sending further scouts through the Barrens.

For Horde druids, marching into Stonetalon Peak to strike down a dryad child of Cenarius illustrates the bitter political tension between faction allegiance and sacred natural ties.
Securing the northern borders of the Barrens is essential for maintaining control over Kalimdor's central plains and protecting fledgling settlements from night elf incursions.
Orcs view Kadrak's decisive offensive as the only suitable answer to territorial intrusion, showing strength rather than allowing the Alliance room to maneuver.

A Friend in Need is an urgent plea for aid from Iverron, a young night elf found suffering from venomous spider bites in Shadowglen. Struck down by the deadly beast Githyiss the Vile, Iverron sends travelers to find Dirania Silvershine before the venom claims him.

Shadowglen's sprawling canopies shelter all manner of wildlife, but the nearby webbed hollows house far darker threats. Ignoring past warnings, Iverron ventured too close to the local webwood caverns and encountered Githyiss the Vile, a vicious spider whose venom quickly overwhelmed the young elf. Stricken with dizziness and failing strength, he is entirely unable to reach safety on his own.

Desperate for survival, Iverron directs any passerby to race back toward the central tree of Aldrassil and alert Dirania Silvershine. Dirania, accustomed to looking out for him and familiar with the hazards of the glen, represents his only hope of preparing a life-saving antidote before the toxin proves fatal.

Iverron's Antidote is an urgent task in Shadowglen to save a poisoned night elf scout. By gathering wild mushrooms, lilies, and spider ichor, adventurers help Dirania Silvershine brew a remedy before the venom takes full hold.

While scouting the boughs of Shadowglen, young Iverron fell victim to the poisonous fangs of the local Webwood spiders. Collapsed and dying, his survival depends entirely on the herbal knowledge of Dirania Silvershine at Aldrassil. With the youth fading fast, she must quickly prepare a specialized concoction to neutralize the aggressive venom coursing through his blood.

Dirania's recipe relies on the restorative flora of Teldrassil balanced against the venom itself. Hyacinth mushrooms, favored by the thieving grell to the south, provide an earthy base, while delicate Moonpetal lilies gathered from tranquil forest pools offer purifying qualities. To finish the draft, a sample of Webwood ichor must be extracted directly from the spiders prowling near Shadowthread Cave to tailor the cure to their specific poison.

This errand tasks an adventurer with racing against time to deliver freshly brewed medicine to a poisoned night elf scout. Stranded outside a spider-infested cave in Shadowglen, Iverron depends entirely on Dirania Silvershine's herbal concoction before the potent mixture loses its efficacy.

Dirania Silvershine crafts the curative brew using freshly harvested venom sacs, lily roots, and hyacinth fungi, but its unstable alchemical nature poses a grave risk. The medicine retains its potency for a mere five minutes after distillation. Anyone carrying the vial must sprint directly from the glade toward the northern heights without hesitation.

Iverron has fallen victim to the Webwood spiders lurking around the barrows and caves of Shadowglen. Washed Ashore is an investigation initiated by Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde in Auberdine on behalf of the Temple of the Moon. Mass strandings of giant sea creatures along the Darkshore coastline have raised alarms among the night elf priesthood in Darnassus. Adventurers are tasked with driving back scavenging murlocs to secure skeletal specimens for study.

Crime and Punishment is an Alliance bounty originating in Darkshire that demands the extrajudicial execution of a grave robber imprisoned within the Stormwind Stockade. Councilman Millstipe issues the contract after the House of Nobles overrides Duskwood's death sentence for Dextren Ward. Carrying out the hit satisfies local vengeance while delivering a sharp warning to the capital's negligent aristocracy.

Duskwood already suffers beneath a shroud of creeping horrors and official indifference from the capital. When Dextren Ward was caught digging up fresh corpses from the Darkshire cemetery to sell to the necromancer Morbent Fel, the town's ruling council showed no mercy. Lord Ello Ebonlocke sentenced the grave robber to beheadment. However, before the axe could fall, the House of Nobles intervened, claiming Ward as an imperial prisoner and transferring him to the high-security cells of the Stormwind Stockade.

To Councilman Millstipe and the grieving citizens of Darkshire, sparing Ward from the headsman's block was an intolerable insult. The nobles in their secure city showed complete disregard for the torment suffered by frontier families whose dead relatives were fed into Fel's dark craft. Frustrated by Stormwind's bureaucratic meddling, Millstipe recruits daring mercenaries to infiltrate the riotous Stockade, assassinate Ward in his cell, and sever his hand as proof of execution.

Gold Dust Exchange is an early bounty offered by Remy "Two Times" out of Goldshire. The nervous broker pays adventurers to pry raw gold dust away from the kobolds infesting the mines across Elwynn Forest. While it provides honest work for fledgling travelers, Remy's curious connections hint that there is more to his hustle than simple metalworking.
A Town of Pockets and Picks

Goldshire sits at the crossroads of Elwynn Forest, where merchants, town guards, and weary travelers mingle. Among them is Remy "Two Times," a shady fellow whose persistent habit of repeating his words masks a shrewd eye for profit. Rather than hiring costly mining teams to extract raw minerals, Remy capitalizes on the wandering adventurers filtering through the Lion's Pride Inn. His proposal is simple: recover the gold dust hoarded by the region's vermin and trade it directly for coin.

Kobolds have thoroughly overrun Elwynn's most valuable subterranean excavations, namely Fargodeep Mine to the south and Jasperlode Mine to the northeast. While chipping through the dark for their beloved candles and shiny baubles, these rat-like tunnelers accumulate residue and flecks of unrefined ore in their pouches. Driving them back serves the kingdom's interest, but collecting their dust turns pest extermination into a lucrative trade.

While Remy claims to pay top coin for pure mercantile reasons, his rewards carry subtle warnings. Upon receiving his dust, he slips his helpers a small token representing his "associates." In an Elwynn increasingly strangled by organized bandits, unpaid stonemasons, and clandestine networks operating in the shadows of Stormwind, Remy's quiet brokers may have plans for that gold that extend far beyond ordinary village commerce.
